findings.title: `as_real` silently rounds integers above 2**53
findings.description: `as_real` calls `float(value)` on any `Integral`, so integers that a float cannot hold are rounded with no signal. `float(2**53 + 1)` is `9007199254740992.0`. Two effects follow. A REAL parameter supplied as `9007199254740993` binds to `…992.0` with no issue raised. `ConfidenceRange(2**53, 2**53 + 1)` is refused with "low must be less than high", although the input range is valid. The docstring does not mention rounding, and no test in `test_value_checks.py` covers an integer above 2**53. Fix: for an exact `Integral`, return `None` when `float(value) != value`, or document the rounding and add a test.

findings.title: `_coerce` has no fallthrough arm, so a new `ParameterType` fails silently
findings.description: The `match` covers `INTEGER` and `REAL` with no `case _`. A new member would fall through and return `None`. `_coerce` already uses `None` to mean "uncoercible value", so a valid supplied value would be reported as `WRONG_TYPE`, and a declaration of the new type would fail with "is not a valid <type>". The message would point at the value, not the missing arm. The return type includes `None`, so the type checker does not flag the gap. `test_parameter_type_has_two_members` catches the new member but does not require the new arm. Fix: add `case _: assert_never(parameter_type)`.

findings.title: The element-loop guard is copied three times with different node sets
findings.description: `ELEMENT_LOOP_NODES` and the AST walk are repeated in `tests/core_model/test_confidence.py:25` (loop check at 133-136) and `tests/core_model/test_labels.py:27` (loop check at 283-285). The copies disagree. `test_import_boundary.py` counts `ast.GeneratorExp` as a loop. The other two exclude it so that `all(...)` over category ids passes. The guard's meaning therefore depends on which file it sits in, and the project rule against duplicated logic applies. Fix: one shared helper that takes the generator rule as a parameter.

findings.title: `LabelVocabulary` is annotated `frozenset[int]` but accepts `set`
findings.description: The field is annotated `frozenset[int]`, but `__post_init__` also accepts `set` and converts it. The `# pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance]` on line 56 hides that the annotation is narrower than the runtime contract. Callers that pass a set need a `reportArgumentType` ignore, as in `test_labels.py:66`. Fix: annotate the field `AbstractSet[int]` and drop the ignore.

findings.title: Module docstring says there are no element loops, but one exists
findings.description: The docstring says "there are no element loops". `LabelVocabulary.__post_init__` runs an element-wise `all(...)` over `category_ids` (lines 64-67). The loop-guard test exempts generator expressions, which is why the claim looks true. Fix: narrow the docstring to the array checks and name the category-id pass.

findings.title: D10 "no canonical type" is checked only by a source-name scan
findings.description: `test_labels_signals_declarations_define_no_canonical_type` looks for a `CANONICAL_TYPE` name in each module's AST and checks no behaviour. Only `display.py` has a behavioural test: `tests/core_model/test_display.py#test_display_hint_is_not_canonical` asserts that `canonicalize` raises. `LabelVocabulary`, `LabelSeries`, `SignalEvent`, `SignalSequence`, `Declarations`, and `ParameterDeclaration` have no such test. Fix: add one parametrized test asserting that `canonicalize` raises `CanonicalFormError` for each new type, matching `test_display.py`.

findings.title: `errors.py` imports upward, and `InvalidParametersError` breaks the error constructor contract
findings.description: Under `TYPE_CHECKING`, `errors.py` imports `ParameterIssue` from `declarations.py`, so the leaf error module depends on a higher layer. Separately, `InvalidParametersError.__init__` (lines 99-110) takes `issues` instead of a message. Helpers typed `error: type[CoreModelError]`, such as `require_instance` in `validation.py`, call `error(message)`. With this class, the string is stored as `issues`, and `str()` then fails with `AttributeError`. No call site does this today. Fix: move `ParameterIssue` and `ParameterIssueKind` into a leaf module, and keep this error out of helper signatures or give it a message-first constructor.

findings.title: Duplicated name and order logic across modules
findings.description: `_require_time_order` repeats the neighbour-order check in `series_index.py#_time_array`. `declarations.py` repeats `require_name(self.name, ...)` in `SeriesOutput`, `LabelOutput`, and `SignalOutput` (lines 126, 140, 154). `value_checks._require_pattern` and `validation.require_nonempty_str` both perform the `type(value) is not str` check. Each repeat is small, but together they break the rule against duplicated logic. Fix: share one non-decreasing check that takes an int64 array, and one name check.

findings.title: `bind_parameters` takes external input and the module does not say which layer validates it
findings.description: The Python rules require Pydantic at external boundaries, and `supplied` is external input. Core Model is kept dependency-free: `tests/core_model/test_import_boundary.py:19` allows only numpy. Validation here is therefore hand-written, and the module docstring does not say which layer applies Pydantic before values reach `bind_parameters`. Fix: state that layer in the module docstring.
